– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The failing test `testLang412Right()` calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight(null, 10, '*')` on a `StrBuilder` instance. The implementation of `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` shows the following key line:

```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
```

This line means when the passed object `obj` is `null`, the method substitutes it with the result of `getNullText()`. The `getNullText()` method simply returns a member variable `nullText`.

The issue described in the bug report states that if `getNullText()` has not been set, then attempting to append a null value with fixed width causes a NullPointerException. Since `getNullText()` returns a member variable `nullText`, if this variable is `null` (which is the default if it is not explicitly set), then `str` will be assigned `null`. The subsequent call `str.length()` will then throw a NullPointerException.

In the test `testLang412Right()`, the `nullText` has not been initialized or set to any default string, so the call `appendFixedWidthPadRight(null, 10, '*')` leads to `str` being null inside the method, causing the NPE when trying to get its length.

This diagnosis aligns exactly with the report that appending a null value causes a null pointer exception if `getNullText()` has not been set.

Recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated and do not mention this null handling issue, so they do not provide additional insight.

The root cause: The method `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object, int, char)` does not defensively handle the scenario when `getNullText()` returns `null`. It directly uses the `nullText` result as a string without null-checking or defaulting it to a non-null value (e.g., empty string or "null"). Thus, when `nullText` is not set (stays null), passing a null object to `appendFixedWidthPadRight` causes a NullPointerException.

A fix would require making `appendFixedWidthPadRight` robust to `getNullText()` returning null, possibly by using a default non-null string value in that case.

The failing test also supports this diagnosis: it simply passes `null` to `appendFixedWidthPadRight`, and the exception occurs due to nullText being unset.

---
